Terrain

Floor level
Rock height
Water level

Levels are in storeys; 0 is the normal floor. Floors at other levels stay walkable, and a one-tile cave bank forms where levels meet (the higher tile becomes the bank). Rock rises one storey per tile; height 2 is the normal cave wall. Water level 0 is a pond with an overworld shoreline; lower water sinks into a pit with cave-wall banks (good for lava).

Textures 6

Paints floors, water and the flat tops of rock. None leaves a rock top black, like the cave walls. Bright grass, path, sand, snow, puddles and lakes get rounded edges and corners automatically on the floor around them, using the same edge tiles as the overworld.

Objects 7

Objects stand on the level of the tile under their corner and block the tiles they cover (flowers, craters and pools stay walkable). R turns the next object.

Previews

The battle preview uses the chosen background and ground, in the day, evening or night palette that matches the lighting. The ball shows how the lighting shades the player, Pokémon and NPCs. Fixed times of day also tint the hideaway map itself.

Hideaway

Adding it to the game

Drag to paint. Hold Shift while dragging to fill a rectangle. Right-click a tile to pick up its terrain, height and texture.

Exit goes in a straight cave wall two storeys above the floor in front of it, with rock on both sides. Every exit leads back to the Underground; players arrive at the first one.

Save the file into tools/underground_block_editor_assets/hideaways, then run py -3 install_hideaways.py in the tools folder.

Encounters

Encounter rate
SlotPokémonMin levelMax levelEncounter chanceSlot ratio

Hideaways work like caves: every floor tile can start a battle, and surfable water uses the water table. Each slot has its own level range. The rate is how often battles start (caves in Platinum use about 10; 0 turns them off). If any slot is empty while the rate is above 0, the installer turns that table off.
